content.text: No audit, inspection, verification, or records-examination right exists anywhere in the agreement, and the only usage-data access provision runs in our favour.

input.quote: e. Access. Client will have access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files in real time via the Interface.
input.rationale: Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verif", "examine", "records", "books" and "monitor" return no audit or verification right running against the Client, and a full read of the two candidate sections confirms this: § 5/§ 6 (COMPENSATION; DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES, p0045–p0047) gives TrueLink no right to audit Client's usage or fees — it instead obliges TrueLink to substantiate its charges to us and caps its rates. § 8 (Client covenants) contains no inspection right; its only access provision (p0053, Limitation on Access) is a Client covenant to restrict access to the Interface, not a Vendor entry right, and the "reasonable access" in p0060 is limited to TrueLink performing Y2K repairs at its own cost. The sole usage-data mechanic, § 2(e) (p0037), grants access to us, not to the Vendor, and because TrueLink hosts the Interface it holds usage data directly, so no audit right is needed. There is therefore no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access exposure to constrain — the position is better than the preferred position (no audit right at all), and inserting one would create Vendor rights against us that do not currently exist. Noted only for the record: because no clause exists, the preferred mechanics (30 days' notice, independent auditor, 5% underpayment cost-shift) are simply inapplicable rather than deficient.
